question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{60}{x}^{3},\, & 2\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<2 \\ h(x),\, & 2\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2\le x\le 4,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ {\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 2\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{2}^{x}\frac{1}{60}{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={\frac{{t}^{4}}{240}|}_{2}^{x} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{240}-\frac{1}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ \frac{{x}^{4}}{240}-\frac{1}{15}, & 2\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$
